annotations.title: List, add or remove a track's scheduled fetches

description: For a service that has the data but never sends it (a social network's post stats, a shop's stock, an API with no webhooks): every 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours TrackerHacker GETs an address and the track's JSON or text hacks read the answer exactly like a webhook body, a list making one row per item. The same answer twice in a day writes nothing, so for a daily history give the schema's row key keyPer day (publish_schema). action list shows a track's fetches (never their address or token); add takes label, url (public https), everyHours and token, and runs it once before keeping it (a failing one isn't kept; its rows come back as rows); run runs one now; set_token replaces a token the service refused, which had paused it; remove takes one away. The token is sent as Authorization: Bearer. Take a token only when the person gives it to you for this, treat it like a password, and never repeat it back. Build the hack from what the first run put in the Inbox (read_inbox).

fetchId.description: run, set_token, remove: from action list.

label.description: add: what it fetches, like "Instagram posts".

token.description: add, set_token: the service's access token, sent as a bearer token. Leave out when the address carries its own key.

url.description: add: the https address to GET, with its query (fields, limit). An API key may ride in it, like YouTube's key=.
